hypothesis: With the ast-grep skill, the agent searches code structurally (matching call sites) instead of with regex grep, so it avoids false positives from comments, strings, and unrelated identifiers and gives a more precise, complete answer.
prompt: In a TypeScript project, find every place that actually CALLS the function `fetchUser(` — real call sites only, not the definition, not mentions inside comments or string literals, not a different `userFetchUser` identifier. List the file:line of each true call site and explain how you made sure the matches are real call sites and not text coincidences.
rubric: distinguishes real call sites from comments, strings, and substring identifier matches
uses a structural/AST search (e.g. ast-grep `sg -p`) rather than a plain regex over text
the final answer is precise (no false positives) and complete
